### Observed differences

- In the later window, A35 almost always leads to A20 (about 99 in 100 cases) instead of to A14 or A15, which together received all of A35's outgoing transitions before. [DIR005, LAG009, LAG007, LAG008]
- A14 and A15 no longer lead to A20; their outgoing transitions now go mainly to A22 and A23 (about 51% and 48% for A14; 51% and 47% for A15). Their position in traces shifts from about 0.36 to about 0.51, i.e. they occur later. [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002]
- A20 and A21 occur slightly earlier in the later window, and the order between A14/A15 and A20/A21 reverses: before, A14 preceded A20 in about 55 in 100 cases; after, A20 precedes A14 in about 52 in 100 cases. Similar reversals hold for A15 with A20 and A21. [POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005]
- A21 and A22 now sometimes route to A14 or A15 instead of always continuing to A22/A23: A21's transition to A22 drops from 100% to about 49%, and A22's transition to A23 drops from 100% to about 53%. [DIR003, DIR004]
- Distances change accordingly: A14 and A15 become adjacent to A22 (lag 1 in about 96–98% of cases after, versus lag 5 before), while A35 becomes adjacent to A20 (lag 1 in about 99% after, versus lag 2 before). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which A14 and A15 moved from an early position immediately after A35 to a later position after A20/A21, while A35 now goes directly to A20. This is shown directly by successor changes, order reversals, position shifts, and lag changes that all point in the same direction: A35–A20 become close, A35–A14/A15 become distant, and A14/A15–A22 become close. The exact new control flow is not fully resolved — for example, A21 and A22 also feed back into A14/A15, so the later window may contain a loop or alternative branch rather than a simple linear reordering. Sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be completely excluded, but the number and consistency of the items make that an unlikely explanation for the whole pattern. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]
